### *class* equate.service.MatchService(\*, sessions=None, cache='default', mk_id=<function MatchService.<lambda>>, field_compare='ratio', on_cost=None, precedence=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

equate’s matching core as stateless + session-scoped JSON-able operations.

Every seam is a keyword argument with a working default:

- `sessions` — where sessions live (any `MutableMapping`; default an in-memory
  dict; pass a pickle-valued `dol` store to persist them);
- `cache` — where stateless match results are cached (default a bounded LRU; pass
  `None` to disable);
- `mk_id` — session-id factory (default `uuid4().hex`);
- `field_compare` — the per-field comparator used in explanations;
- `on_cost` — `(tier, seconds, items)` hook called on every accounted tier;
- `precedence` — edit sources ranked most authoritative first (`('human',
  'llm')`): a less authoritative edit never overrides a more authoritative one
  (default `None`: the latest edit wins, whoever made it).

#### candidates(session_id, item, , k=None)

Item `item`’s top-k candidates (best first), with explanations.

With `k` (larger or smaller than the session’s), the item’s top-k is
**refreshed** from the cached scores and stored — no re-scoring.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)

#### close_session(session_id)

Forget a session. Returns whether it existed.

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

#### edit(session_id, edits)

Apply `edits` ([`Edit`](_autosummary/equate.service.html.md#equate.service.Edit) or dicts) and re-optimize the assignment.

Atomic: if an edit is invalid or the edits leave no feasible assignment, a
`ValueError` is raised and the session is unchanged. One constrained LAP over the
cached scores — an edit is a cheap re-solve, never a re-score. Concurrent edits of
one session (in this process) are serialized, so none is lost.

* **Return type:**
  [`EditResult`](_autosummary/equate.service.html.md#equate.service.EditResult)

#### label(session_id, item, candidate, is_match, , source='human')

Record an oracle label and apply it (a match confirms, a non-match rejects).

Returns the edit result and the next active-learning [`Query`](_autosummary/equate.service.html.md#equate.service.Query) — the most
uncertain item no label has decided yet (`None` when none is left).

* **Return type:**
  [`LabelResult`](_autosummary/equate.service.html.md#equate.service.LabelResult)

#### match(A, B, , featurize=None, compare=None, block=None, how='assign', threshold=None, sense=None)

Match two collections (stateless). Mirrors `equate.match()`.

`how` is `'assign'` (optimal 1:1), `'greedy'`, `'stable'`, `'soft'` or
`'cluster'` (then `groups` lists the entity clusters over the pooled `A + B`
indices, `B` offset by `len(A)`). Pairs below `threshold` (above it, for a
`'minimize'` sense) are dropped. Results are cached by content.

* **Return type:**
  [`MatchResult`](_autosummary/equate.service.html.md#equate.service.MatchResult)

#### next_query(session_id)

The next pair to label: uncertainty sampling over the not-yet-decided items.

An item is decided once it is confirmed. The pair offered is the item’s current
match when it has one, else its best candidate that is neither rejected for it nor
confirmed for another item — so labelling never steals a confirmed match back and
forth. An item with no such candidate left is skipped.

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Query`](_autosummary/equate.service.html.md#equate.service.Query)]

#### open_session(A, B, , k=5, featurize=None, compare=None, block=None, sense=None, floor=None)

Score `A` against `B` once and open an interactive review session.

The session keeps each item’s top-`k` candidates and the optimal 1:1
assignment; every later edit re-solves from these cached scores.

`floor` is the lowest acceptable score (the highest acceptable distance for a
`'minimize'` sense). Pairs past it are not candidates at all: never proposed,
never offered for review, and a reject never pushes an item onto one — the item is
left unmatched. Like blocking (D11), the assignment is then *lexicographic*: as
many acceptable pairs as possible, then the best total score — so a floor can
change the opening assignment, not just trim it. That is unlike
[`match()`](_autosummary/equate.service.html.md#equate.service.MatchService.match)’s `threshold`, which solves first and then drops weak pairs.

* **Return type:**
  [`SessionView`](_autosummary/equate.service.html.md#equate.service.SessionView)

#### review(session_id, , n=None, include_confirmed=True)

The review queue: items ordered most-uncertain first (smallest margin).

Confirmed items come last (a human already decided them); `include_confirmed=
False` drops them. Each [`ReviewItem`](_autosummary/equate.service.html.md#equate.service.ReviewItem) carries its top-k candidates with
field-diff explanations — everything a review row needs.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)

#### view(session_id, , n=None)

The current state of a session (`n` caps the review queue length).

* **Return type:**
  [`SessionView`](_autosummary/equate.service.html.md#equate.service.SessionView)

### *class* equate.service.PairView(item, candidate, left, right, score, status='proposed')

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A matched pair: indices, both objects, the score, and whether a user fixed it.

### *class* equate.service.Query(item, left, candidate, margin)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

An active-learning query: the pair an oracle should label next.

### *class* equate.service.ReviewItem(item, left, assigned, status, margin, candidates)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

One row of the review queue: an item, its current match and its alternatives.

`margin` is the top-1/top-2 score gap (`None` when there is no rival) — small
means ambiguous, which is why the queue puts it first.

### *class* equate.service.Session(session_id, store, k, assignment, edits=list(), labels=list(), accounting=Accounting(), floor=None, version=0)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Server-side session state. Not a boundary type: [`SessionView`](_autosummary/equate.service.html.md#equate.service.SessionView) is its view.

The mutable part only — the edit log, labels, assignment and candidates — saved after
every change; `A`, `B` and `scores` read through the attached
[`SessionData`](_autosummary/equate.service.html.md#equate.service.SessionData). Everything is plain data, so both pickle into any `dol` store
passed as `MatchService(sessions=...)`. `version` counts saves: a save that finds
a newer version in the store raises [`SessionConflict`](_autosummary/equate.service.html.md#equate.service.SessionConflict) instead of overwriting a
change made by another process.

### *exception* equate.service.SessionConflict

Bases: [`RuntimeError`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError)

The session changed in the store since it was read (an HTTP 409): another process
saved it first. Re-read the session and retry the edit.

### *class* equate.service.SessionData(A, B, scores)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

The immutable part of a session: both collections and their score matrix.

Written once, when the session opens; every later save writes only the small
[`Session`](_autosummary/equate.service.html.md#equate.service.Session) state — not the `n × m` scores (equate#23).

### *exception* equate.service.SessionNotFound

Bases: [`KeyError`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#KeyError)

No session with that id (an HTTP 404).

### *class* equate.service.SessionView(session_id, n_left, n_right, sense, k, assignment, review, edits, labels, accounting, floor=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A session’s state: its current assignment and the review queue to work through.

### *class* equate.service.TierCost(calls=0, seconds=0.0, items=0)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

What one tier (`score`, `match`, `reoptimize`, …) has cost so far.

### equate.service.explain_pair(left, right, score, , field_compare='ratio')

A structured [`Explanation`](_autosummary/equate.base.html.md#equate.base.Explanation) of a pair: a per-field diff.

Records (mappings) are compared field by field over the union of their keys; any other
object is one field named `value`. A side that is absent, `None` or `''` has no
similarity (`None`): missing is not the same as different. `details['fields']` is a list of
[`FieldDiff`](_autosummary/equate.service.html.md#equate.service.FieldDiff) dicts — the payload a UI renders as a side-by-side diff.

```pycon
>>> e = explain_pair({'name': 'Jon'}, {'name': 'Jon', 'city': 'Paris'}, 0.8)
>>> [(f['field'], f['similarity']) for f in e.details['fields']]
[('name', 1.0), ('city', None)]
```

### equate.service.json_schemas()

JSON Schemas of the boundary types, keyed by type name.

Generated from the dataclasses with `pydantic` (part of `equate[service]`). The UI
keeps a snapshot of the *field names* (`ui/src/schema/fields.json`) and a test on
each side fails when the Python types and the Zod schemas drift apart.

### equate.service.mk_app(service=None, , cors_origins=('http://localhost:5173', 'http://127.0.0.1:5173'), ui_dir=None, api_prefix='/api')

Mount a [`MatchService`](_autosummary/equate.service.html.md#equate.service.MatchService) as an HTTP API (FastAPI, built with `qh`).

Routes (JSON in, JSON out):

```default
POST   /match                                       stateless match
POST   /sessions                                    open a review session
GET    /sessions/{session_id}                       session state + review queue
DELETE /sessions/{session_id}                       close it
GET    /sessions/{session_id}/candidates/{item}     an item's top-k
POST   /sessions/{session_id}/candidates/{item}     refresh it with {"k": ...}
POST   /sessions/{session_id}/edits                 {"edits": [...]} -> re-optimized
POST   /sessions/{session_id}/label                 oracle label -> next query
GET    /sessions/{session_id}/next                  the next query to label
```

An unknown session is a 404, a session another process changed first a 409, an
invalid edit or unknown strategy a 422. Handlers run in a worker thread, so a long
scoring call does not block other requests. The default in-memory session store is
per process: with several server processes (`uvicorn --workers N`) pass a shared
store, `MatchService(sessions=<dol store>)`, or a request can reach a process that
does not hold its session. `cors_origins`
lets the review UI’s dev server (vite, port 5173) call it; pass `()` to disable.
Requires `pip install 'equate[service]'`.

`ui_dir` serves the review UI from the same app: a built bundle (`cd ui && npm run
build` → `ui/dist`) is mounted at `/` and the routes above move under
`api_prefix` (default `/api`, the path the UI calls — as its dev proxy does), so
one process and one origin serve both; the API’s docs are at `{api_prefix}/docs`.
The bundle has its API path baked in at build time, so a different `api_prefix`
needs a UI built with the same `VITE_EQUATE_API`.

### equate.service.record_text(obj)

Text of `obj`: a mapping’s non-empty values joined by spaces, else `str(obj)`.

```pycon
>>> record_text({'name': 'Jon Smith', 'city': 'Paris', 'zip': None})
'Jon Smith Paris'
>>> record_text(42)
'42'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### equate.service.serve(, host='127.0.0.1', port=8000, service=None, ui_dir=None)

Run the HTTP service with uvicorn (`python -m equate.service serve`).

With `ui_dir` (`python -m equate.service serve ui=ui/dist`) it also serves the
built review UI, at `http://host:port/`.

### equate.service.to_jsonable(obj)

Convert a boundary dataclass (or nested containers of them) to plain JSON data.

Non-finite floats become `None` (JSON has no `inf`/`nan`); tuples become lists;
numpy scalars become Python numbers.


# _autosummary/equate.util.html.md

# equate.util

Utils for equate.

### Functions

| `ensure_sparse`(matrix)                                                                           |                                                                                                                                                       |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`greedy_matching`](_autosummary/equate.util.html.md#equate.util.greedy_matching)(similarity_matrix)               | Greedy Algorithm: Iteratively picks the highest similarity pair and removes the matched items from the pool.                                          |
| [`hungarian_matching`](_autosummary/equate.util.html.md#equate.util.hungarian_matching)(similarity_matrix, \*[, ...]) | Hungarian Algorithm (Optimal Matching): Finds the optimal 1:1 assignment, minimizing the total cost (equivalently, maximizing the total similarity).  |
| [`kuhn_munkres_matching`](_autosummary/equate.util.html.md#equate.util.kuhn_munkres_matching)(similarity_matrix, \*)     | Kuhn-Munkres Algorithm: Another implementation of the Hungarian algorithm using the `networkx` package (requires the optional `equate[graph]` extra). |
| [`match_greedily`](_autosummary/equate.util.html.md#equate.util.match_greedily)(keys, values, \*[, ...])          | Generates the best (key, value) matches of each key of keys with a value of values.                                                                   |
| [`match_keys_to_values`](_autosummary/equate.util.html.md#equate.util.match_keys_to_values)(keys, values[, ...])        | Match each key to a value via a similarity matrix and a matcher.                                                                                      |
| [`maximal_matching`](_autosummary/equate.util.html.md#equate.util.maximal_matching)(similarity_matrix)              | Maximal Matching in Bipartite Graph: Finds a maximal matching in a bipartite graph.                                                                   |
| [`mk_text_to_vect`](_autosummary/equate.util.html.md#equate.util.mk_text_to_vect)(\*learn_texts)                   | Legacy grub-backed TF-IDF featurizer (requires the optional `equate[grub]` extra).                                                                    |
| [`similarity_matrix`](_autosummary/equate.util.html.md#equate.util.similarity_matrix)(keys, values, \*[, ...])       | Return a matrix of the similarity of the keys to the values.                                                                                          |
| [`stable_marriage_matching`](_autosummary/equate.util.html.md#equate.util.stable_marriage_matching)(similarity_matrix, \*)  | Stable Marriage Problem (Gale-Shapley Algorithm): Solves the stable marriage problem, ensuring a stable matching.                                     |
| `transform_text`(text, transformer)                                                               |                                                                                                                                                       |

### equate.util.greedy_matching(similarity_matrix)

Greedy Algorithm: Iteratively picks the highest similarity pair and removes the
matched items from the pool.

* **Parameters:**
  **similarity_matrix** – A sparse matrix of similarities.
* **Returns:**
  List of tuples (row_index, col_index) for matched pairs.

### equate.util.hungarian_matching(similarity_matrix, , sense='maximize', cost_matrix=None)

Hungarian Algorithm (Optimal Matching): Finds the optimal 1:1 assignment,
minimizing the total cost (equivalently, maximizing the total similarity).

* **Parameters:**
  * **similarity_matrix** – A matrix of scores. `sense='maximize'` treats them as
    similarities (higher = better, the default); `sense='minimize'` treats them
    as costs/distances. The conversion goes through the `to_cost` SSOT.
  * **cost_matrix** – An explicit cost matrix to use instead (overrides `sense`).
* **Returns:**
  An iterator of (row_index, col_index) tuples for matched pairs.

### equate.util.kuhn_munkres_matching(similarity_matrix, , sense='maximize')

Kuhn-Munkres Algorithm: Another implementation of the Hungarian algorithm using
the `networkx` package (requires the optional `equate[graph]` extra).

* **Parameters:**
  **similarity_matrix** – A matrix of scores (see `sense`); converted to edge
  costs via the `to_cost` SSOT.
* **Returns:**
  List of tuples (row_index, col_index) for matched pairs.

### equate.util.match_greedily(keys, values, , score_func=None, minimum_score=-inf)

Generates the best (key, value) matches of each key of keys with a value of
values. The score_func is used to gauge the strength of a match. If not provided,
the default score_func is `difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, a, b).ratio()` — a
normalized measure of matching subsequences in [0, 1] (higher is more alike).

```pycon
>>> keys = ['apple', 'banana', 'carrot']
>>> values = ['car', 'app', 'carob', 'cabana']
>>> dict(match_greedily(keys, values))
{'apple': 'app', 'banana': 'cabana', 'carrot': 'carob'}
```

### equate.util.match_keys_to_values(keys, values, obj_to_vect=None, similarity_func=None, matcher=<function hungarian_matching>)

Match each key to a value via a similarity matrix and a matcher.

Builds `similarity_matrix(keys, values, ...)` (TF-IDF + cosine by default) and
applies `matcher` (optimal Hungarian assignment by default), yielding
`(key, value)` pairs. `obj_to_vect` and `similarity_func` default to the
lazily-resolved TF-IDF featurizer and cosine comparator when left as `None`.

### equate.util.maximal_matching(similarity_matrix)

Maximal Matching in Bipartite Graph: Finds a maximal matching in a bipartite graph.
See [https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/maximum-bipartite-matching/](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/maximum-bipartite-matching/).

Accepts a dense array, a **sparse (blocked)** matrix, or a
[`ScoreMatrix`](_autosummary/equate.base.html.md#equate.base.ScoreMatrix). Only *candidate* cells become graph edges, so a
structurally-absent cell is not an edge at all: it can be neither preferred nor
assigned, and max-cardinality is maximized over real candidates (D11). Reading the
matrix cell-by-cell instead would turn every hole into a real weight-`0.0` edge —
which silently beats any negative similarity.

* **Parameters:**
  **similarity_matrix** – A dense/sparse matrix of similarities, or a `ScoreMatrix`.
* **Returns:**
  Iterator of tuples (row_index, col_index) for matched pairs.

### equate.util.mk_text_to_vect(\*learn_texts)

Legacy grub-backed TF-IDF featurizer (requires the optional `equate[grub]`
extra). The default text featurizer is now equate’s pure numpy/scipy char-n-gram
TF-IDF — see [`equate.featurize.mk_tfidf()`](_autosummary/equate.featurize.html.md#equate.featurize.mk_tfidf).

### equate.util.similarity_matrix(keys, values, , obj_to_vect=None, similarity_func=None)

Return a matrix of the similarity of the keys to the values.

By default the featurizer is learned from `keys` and `values` using equate’s
pure numpy/scipy char-n-gram TF-IDF ([`equate.featurize`](_autosummary/equate.featurize.html.md#module-equate.featurize)), and similarity is
cosine (`equate._vector.cosine_similarity()`) — no scikit-learn or grub needed.
Pass `obj_to_vect` to use a different batch featurizer (precomputed embeddings, or
a registered name resolved via `equate.featurize.resolve_featurizer`), and
`similarity_func` to use a different similarity.

```pycon
>>> keys = ['apple pie', 'apple crumble', 'banana split']
>>> values = ['american pie', 'big apple', 'american girl', 'banana republic']
>>> m = similarity_matrix(keys, values)
>>> m.round(2).tolist()
[[0.32, 0.42, 0.01, 0.0], [0.04, 0.35, 0.01, 0.02], [0.03, 0.04, 0.02, 0.44]]
```

### equate.util.stable_marriage_matching(similarity_matrix, , sense='maximize')

Stable Marriage Problem (Gale-Shapley Algorithm):
Solves the stable marriage problem, ensuring a stable matching. Note this
optimizes *stability* (no blocking pair), not total score, and is
proposer-optimal / receiver-pessimal — so it can differ from the optimal
assignment found by `hungarian_matching`.
See: [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stable_marriage_problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stable_marriage_problem)

* **Parameters:**
  **similarity_matrix** – A matrix of scores (see `sense`); preferences are
  ranked by the `to_cost` distance, so higher similarity is more preferred.
* **Returns:**
  List of tuples (row_index, col_index) for matched pairs.

# ai-agents.html.md

# For AI agents

`equate` ships artifacts for coding agents alongside its code. This page lists
them, says where each lives in the repository, and points at the
machine-readable copies of this documentation.

## Skills

Skills are folders holding a `SKILL.md` (the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format): a description that tells an agent when to use it and a body with the procedure. Install one into your agent with `gh skill` (any host: `--agent claude-code`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `codex`, `gemini`), or use the copy bundled in the wheel.

### `equate-dev-add-strategy`

How to add a new strategy to equate — a featurizer, comparator, blocker, matcher, or clusterer — the equate way. Covers picking the stage/subpackage, satisfying the callable protocol + declaring strategy metadata, registering it in the name-keyed registry with a LAZY factory, wiring an optional heavy dependency as a pip extra with a check_requirements-style error (never a raw ImportError), and adding deterministic tests that skip when the optional dep is absent. Triggers when adding, registering, or wrapping a matching strategy or a third-party library behind an equate extra.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/equate equate-dev-add-strategy --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`skills/equate-dev-add-strategy`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/equate/tree/HEAD/skills/equate-dev-add-strategy).

### `equate-dev-architecture`

Read before designing, reviewing, or modifying equate’s core matching architecture. Covers the featurize→compare→match/resolve pipeline, the module layout, the stage protocols, the resolved score-sense / ScoreMatrix / structured-return contracts, and the “own the orchestration, wrap the libraries” rule. Triggers when working on equate’s public API, adding or adjusting a pipeline stage, choosing where a concern lives, or making any design decision about the matching core. The module map describes the shipped code; open issues hold what is still to build.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/equate equate-dev-architecture --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`skills/equate-dev-architecture`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/equate/tree/HEAD/skills/equate-dev-architecture).

## Instruction files

Files agents read before working in this repository.

- [`.claude/CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/equate/tree/HEAD/.claude/CLAUDE.md): read by Claude Code

## Machine-readable documentation

This site publishes the same documentation in forms that fit an agent’s context window:

- [`llms.txt`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/equate/llms.txt): an index of every page with a one-line description ([llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format)
- [`equate.md`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/equate/equate.md): the whole documentation as one Markdown file
- `<page>.html.md`: a rendered Markdown twin of every page, advertised from each page’s `<head>` with `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`
- [`objects.inv`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/equate/objects.inv): the Sphinx inventory: a symbol-to-URL index (`sphobjinv convert plain objects.inv -`)
